seo.title: GDPR-Compliant Analytics: No Cookies, No Consent Banner, One DPA
seo.description: GDPR-compliant web and product analytics without cookie banners or US data routing. Hosted on Hetzner in Germany, cookieless by default, one DPA included, and fully self-hostable on your own infrastructure.

hero.heading: GDPR-compliant analytics that doesn't need a consent banner
hero.subheading: Google Analytics needs explicit consent, and banner rejection rates wreck attribution. Most US tools route EU data through US servers. OpenPanel is cookieless, hosted in Germany, and self-hostable for full data sovereignty. No banner, no transfer risk, one DPA.

problem.title: Why most analytics tools are a GDPR liability
problem.intro: The analytics stack most teams default to creates GDPR compliance work that scales worse than the tools themselves.

items.title: GA4 requires explicit consent, which most users decline
items.description: Consent banner dismissal and rejection rates routinely run 30–60%. That means up to half your traffic is invisible to GA4 by design, your conversion attribution is broken, and you're paying for a tool you can't use on the data that matters most.

items.title: US-based tools mean Schrems II risk
items.description: Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog Cloud, and Heap all process EU data on US infrastructure. The EU-US Data Privacy Framework patched the legal hole but EU DPAs continue to scrutinize US transfers. One adequacy challenge and your processor list is suddenly a compliance problem.

items.title: Every processor needs its paperwork
items.description: Each SaaS analytics tool you use as a processor needs a signed DPA, and US vendors add SCCs and transfer impact assessments on top. Most engineering teams do not track which tools have signed what, so a first GDPR audit finds gaps.

items.title: Cookie consent rejection = no data
items.description: Even when banners show, modern users dismiss them fast. The data you're collecting is the data from users who didn't notice the banner, not your real audience. Cookieless analytics is the structural fix; bolting consent on top of GA4 is not.

features.title: How OpenPanel makes GDPR analytics painless
features.intro: Architecture-level decisions, not consent-banner workarounds, that put OpenPanel inside GDPR's legitimate-interest basis from the start.

items.title: Cookieless tracking by default
items.description: A visitor is a daily-rotating salted hash of IP, user agent and site. No cookies, no localStorage, no persistent identifier. PECR does not apply and no banner is needed for analytics.

items.title: EU-hosted cloud
items.description: OpenPanel Cloud runs on Hetzner in Germany, with backups on Cloudflare R2 inside the EU. Your event data does not cross the Atlantic, and a GDPR data processing agreement is included at /dpa.

items.title: Self-host for total data sovereignty
items.description: Run OpenPanel on your own infrastructure (Docker Compose: ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis, one install script). Your servers, your data, your jurisdiction. No third-party processor at all.

items.title: No raw IP on events
items.description: The IP is used once, for the country and city lookup and the daily device hash, and is not stored on events. Nothing to configure.

items.title: Open-source codebase you can audit
items.description: The platform is AGPL-3.0 and the SDKs are MIT. Show your DPO which fields are collected, how the visitor id is hashed and where it is stored. The privacy page lists every sub-processor.

items.title: Data subject requests
items.description: Export every event for a profile through the REST API for an Article 15 request. For erasure, delete the profile's rows in your own ClickHouse when self-hosted, or ask us on Cloud.

items.title: No third-country data transfers
items.description: EU cloud or self-host means EU-only processing. No Standard Contractual Clauses, no transfer impact assessments, no chapter V exposure.

items.title: Documented data flow
items.description: Open code, a public sub-processor list and a DPA you can read before you sign up. Hand the privacy page to your auditor; there is no proprietary black box to defend.

benefits.title: Why privacy-conscious teams pick OpenPanel
benefits.intro: The compliance benefits show up in your data quality, your legal review cycle, and your audit response time.

items.title: Get the real attribution picture
items.description: Cookieless tracking captures all your traffic, not just consenting users. Conversion attribution, funnel analysis, and retention metrics finally reflect reality.

items.title: No DPA paperwork burden
items.description: Self-hosted OpenPanel is software you run, not a processor; there is nothing to sign. Cloud users sign one DPA with OpenPanel instead of a stack of them with US vendors.

items.title: Pass GDPR audits without scrambling
items.description: Architecture-level privacy means the auditor's questions ('What's the lawful basis? Where's the data? Who's the processor?') have one-line answers.

items.title: Compliance that scales with the company
items.description: Stricter contracts, EU public-sector work or a data residency clause need no re-platforming: self-host and the data never leaves your network.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about GDPR-compliant analytics
faqs.intro: Common questions from privacy engineers, DPOs, and founders evaluating OpenPanel for EU compliance.

items.question: Do I still need a cookie consent banner with OpenPanel?
items.answer: Not for product analytics. OpenPanel's cookieless mode stores no cookies and no persistent identifier, so PECR does not apply and GDPR consent is not required; legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)) is the usual lawful basis. Cookie-based features you add yourself, such as advertising tags, still need consent.

items.question: What's the lawful basis for processing without consent?
items.answer: Legitimate interest under GDPR Article 6(1)(f). OpenPanel keeps no cookies, no persistent identifier and no raw IP on events, so the balancing test is straightforward: minimal data, no profiling of anonymous visitors, transparent purpose. Document the legitimate interest assessment and you are covered. Once you call identify() with a user id you are processing personal data as you already do in your product.

items.question: Does OpenPanel solve Schrems II?
items.answer: OpenPanel Cloud runs on Hetzner in Germany with EU backups, so no transfer to the US occurs. Self-hosted is entirely on your infrastructure, so the question never arises. Compare this with tools that process EU data on US servers and need SCCs and transfer impact assessments.

items.question: Do I need to sign a DPA with OpenPanel?
items.answer: If you self-host, no: OpenPanel is software, not a service provider. If you use OpenPanel Cloud, yes, one DPA, published at /dpa. Either way it is simpler than a stack of US vendors each needing their own DPA and SCCs.

items.question: How does data subject access / erasure (Articles 15 & 17) work?
items.answer: Access (Article 15): the REST API exports every event for a profileId, and the profile page shows the same data. Erasure (Article 17): when self-hosted you delete the profile's rows in ClickHouse; on Cloud you ask us and we remove them. Wire the export into your existing request workflow.

items.question: What about HIPAA and CCPA?
items.answer: OpenPanel does not offer HIPAA compliance and cannot sign a Business Associate Agreement, on Cloud or otherwise. If you handle health data, self-host: no third party sits in the data path, so no business associate relationship exists, and you control retention. Be careful with session replay (it records the DOM) and with PHI in URLs or event properties, which are stored as sent. For CCPA, the cookieless setup covers the 'Do Not Sell' and 'Limit Use' rights without code changes.

items.question: How does OpenPanel compare to Plausible and Matomo for GDPR?
items.answer: All three are cookieless and EU-hostable. Plausible is the simplest but has no product analytics (no retention, cohorts, user profiles or replay). Matomo has more features but uses cookies by default (switchable) and sells advanced features as paid plugins. OpenPanel sits between them: simpler than Matomo, deeper than Plausible. See /articles/self-hosted-web-analytics for a feature-by-feature comparison.

items.question: Is OpenPanel SOC 2 certified?
items.answer: No. OpenPanel Cloud is not SOC 2 certified. For workloads that require certification, self-host on infrastructure that already has it: the codebase is open, and you control every access boundary.
